title: fix: preserve reasoning settings in parallel OpenAI requests
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an overlapping OpenAI Responses SSE request loses saved reasoning-effort controls when another request in the same session owns the continuation cache.

## User Impact

Matching conversation history keeps its original prompt prefix and reasoning changes during parallel requests.

## Why This Change Was Made

The request preparation now restores persisted effort controls even when no continuation claim is available. The existing cache owner still controls continuation state. Production code decreases by one line.

## Evidence

The regression uses the real OpenAI SDK and captures serialized HTTP requests at a local server. It establishes low-to-high reasoning history, holds one request at response acceptance, and admits another request in the same session. Before the fix, the concurrent request sent only the current medium effort; afterward, it preserves the original low effort and both historical controls.

- Focused transport and reasoning suites: 47 tests passed.
- `pnpm test packages/ai/src/transports/openai-responses-client.continuation.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 14 tests passed, 5.52 seconds wrapper wall time; 2.72 seconds Vitest duration.
- Targeted formatting, lint, assertion-safety ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed. The complete packages test type graph passes after the annotation correction. Fresh isolated P2 review found no actionable findings.
- The existing extension-test boundary suite passed all 20 cases.
- Live OpenAI contract proof at `a70d2b1`: four requests returned HTTP 200 and completed normally in 5.48 seconds. The held and concurrent serialized histories matched; the concurrent request retained low root effort plus high and medium controls without `previous_response_id`. The final test-only `satisfies` correction leaves the production request bytes unchanged.
- The first live attempt also completed all four responses normally, but its proof helper failed while draining cloned SSE responses; underlying clone error cause was not retained. An outgoing-request-only capture rerun passed. No provider diagnosis is inferred from that fixture failure.

The first hosted CI run found a plugin-source fixture import and an undocumented existing SDK input-item cast. A separate repair removes the cross-boundary import, selects a registered compatible model through the standalone catalog normalizer, and documents why validated reasoning controls preserve the SDK request invariant. The next CI run passed those boundary and assertion checks, then exposed a fixture type annotation widening an absent service tier to the SDK nullable union. A separate test-only repair uses `satisfies` to preserve the inferred request shape at the public stream boundary. Final-head CI run [38172089639](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38172089639) passed all gates in 616 seconds of wall time; the previously failing test-type stripe passed in 309 seconds.
